answer: Escrowed identity seasoning: new identities post an opal escrow that releases only after N interactions with distinct counterparties, each scored by a reef of independent validators who sample behavior. The escrow grows superlinearly with identity count per operator, and a prism review flags correlated patterns, forfeiting escrow. An attacker running k sybils pays escalating escrow plus forfeiture risk on every detected cluster, making mass identity creation costlier than honest participation.
